title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, December 2026 — the pair's half whose collection window actually spans the 12-11 cliff, 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/manufacturing-business-outlook-survey — the Philadelphia Fed's own MBOS page, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 277,643 bytes). Its Release Calendar panel publishes only the NEXT TWO releases and enumerates exactly those: 'Sep 17 2026 — September Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey — 8:30 a.m.' and 'Oct 15 2026 — October Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey — 8:30 a.m.' December 2026 is NOT enumerated from the primary and this date is therefore a RULE-REPRODUCED estimate, not a read one: both enumerated observations are the third Thursday of their month (September 2026 Thursdays are 3/10/17/24, third = 17; October's are 1/8/15/22/29, third = 15), and December 2026's Thursdays are 3/10/17/24, third = 17. The bank's 'See full calendar' link (philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/data-release-schedule) returns HTTP 200 at 18,472 bytes of JavaScript shell with no readable schedule text, so no further enumeration was reachable this session. The date is also asserted independently by the sibling ledger docs/research/events/philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17.md, whose quarter-horizon call names '12-17' — which is corroboration from this repo, not a second primary. Filed estimate on three counts: the rule-reproduced date, the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts having no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane not self-confirming an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the empire-state-mfg-2026-12-15 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09. Filed because this ledger's central finding INVERTS the pair's ordering for December, and the calendar cannot see the half that matters. The New York Fed's published collection rule ('sent on the first day of each month... Most are completed by the tenth, although surveys are accepted until the fifteenth') puts Empire's December bulk window at Dec 1-10, closing ONE DAY BEFORE government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11 / cr-expiry-2026-12-11 (both high, estimate), with its acceptance tail truncated by the 12-15 release itself. So Empire's December print is a PRE-cliff snapshot, and the proposal that filed Empire's December entry was wrong to call it the first post-cliff read. Philly's own collection window is NOT reachable — its methodology page returns the same JavaScript shell — but its release is two days later on a survey the sibling ledgers infer collects roughly through the release week, which makes the 12-17 edition the earlier of the pair's two December prints whose respondents can have seen a lapse at all. If the pair is to be read for a post-cliff signal, this is the half to read, and the calendar tracked it nowhere. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same grounds as every sibling regional-survey entry: a three-state qualitative diffusion index, no house playbook keyed to regional surveys, no tracked name carrying a Third District manufacturing channel. Whoever writes the canonical philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17.json owns (a) re-verifying the date once the Philadelphia Fed's rolling two-release panel reaches December, since this session could only reproduce it by rule, and (b) reading the bank's actual collection window from a released December report rather than inheriting the sibling's inference. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and this ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
